summary: Design and govern internal talent marketplaces with practical skills taxonomies, gig workflows, dashboards, and pilot plans. Enrol today.
lede: This course on internal talent marketplaces and skills-based workforce mobility shows how to turn fragmented workforce information into credible opportunities for gigs, secondments, project assignments, and career movement. You will learn to classify skills, verify proficiency, match people to work fairly, and measure the outcomes of internal movement. You will practise building a focused skills taxonomy, creating assignment briefs, applying transparent matching and approval rules, and connecting marketplace activity with succession, development, and performance reviews. The course also covers practical piloting, data governance, dashboard design, and the evaluation of technology options without making a platform a prerequisite.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to move scarce skills across departments, programmes, business units, or public service functions without relying solely on external hiring. It suits beginner-to-intermediate practitioners with access to workforce information and responsibility for talent, organizational development, reform, or HR transformation.
prerequisites: You should have working knowledge of HR operations, talent development, organizational design, workforce planning, or public service and NGO programme management. Familiarity with spreadsheets is useful, but coding is not required. Advanced platform configuration, production AI model development, and enterprise HRIS integration are introduced at conceptual or operational application level rather than taught as technical engineering.
